subject: Franska
title: Family and numbers
sourceSummary: Family words, possessive pronouns, and the numbers 0–60.

questions.opener: Compare with "le frère", which you might already know.
questions.explanation: "La sœur" means sister. "Le frère" means brother.

questions.opener: The word is plural and covers both sides of the family.
questions.explanation: "Le grand-père" is grandfather and "la grand-mère" is grandmother. "Les grands-parents" in the plural means grandparents together.

questions.prompt: Choose the right word: "___ mère s'appelle Rosa." (My mom's name is Rosa.)
questions.opener: "Mère" is feminine — but "my" has a special form before a vowel sound.
questions.explanation: In front of a word starting with a vowel sound (like "mère"), "mon" is used instead of "ma", even though the word is feminine — it's easier to pronounce. "Mes" is plural, "ton" is "your".

questions.prompt: How do you write the number 15 in letters?
questions.opener: 15 is one of the compound numbers between 11 and 16.
"Et" (and) is only used with one in compound numbers.
questions.explanation: "Trente" is 30 and "un" is 1, joined with "et" (and): "trente et un" = 31. The same pattern applies to 21 (vingt et un) and 41 (quarante et un).

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Mon frère s'appelle Sofia et elle a quatorze ans." (The name refers to a girl.)
questions.opener: The word for brother and sister changes with gender.
questions.answer: Ma sœur s'appelle Sofia et elle a quatorze ans.
steps: Sofia is a girl's name, so it should be "sœur" (sister), not "frère" (brother).
Since "sœur" is feminine and starts with a consonant sound, the possessive becomes "ma", not "mon".
The rest is correct: "s'appelle Sofia et elle a quatorze ans" (is named Sofia and is fourteen years old).

questions.prompt: Which family words, possessive pronouns, and numbers should you know at grade 7 level in French?
questions.opener: Family, who it belongs to, and being able to count to sixty.
questions.answer: Family: la mère/le père = mom/dad · le frère/la sœur = brother/sister · le grand-père/la grand-mère = grandfather/grandmother · le fils/la fille = son/daughter · le cousin/la cousine = cousin. Possessives: mon/ma/mes = my · ton/ta/tes = your · son/sa/ses = his/her. (Mon/ton/son are also used for feminine words starting with a vowel sound.) Numbers: 0 zéro, 1 un, 5 cinq, 10 dix, 11 onze, 15 quinze, 20 vingt, 21 vingt et un, 30 trente, 31 trente et un, 50 cinquante, 60 soixante.
